sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Chemkart has a credible nutrition-ingredient franchise and a funded manufacturing expansion, but profits have persistently outrun cash. FY26 group revenue was ₹214.83 crore and owner PAT ₹19.66 crore; actual CFO was negative ₹2.73 crore, including ₹14.74 crore paid customs duty carried as recoverable. The funded conditional base gives 18.91% annual return without customs recovery, while execution and downside funding remain material. BQS 4.98, capped GQS 5.00 and conditional IAS 5.60 support a watchlist assessment, not a high-conviction purchase. Headline bank/liquid-fund balances are not all surplus: project earmarking, LC margins and opening tax reduce freely deployable cash. A positive management quarter does not yet demonstrate a durable cash compounder.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Review cutoff: 20 October 2026; BSE SME544442, ISININE0VWL01017, listed 14 July 2025. Accounts use Indian GAAP under Accounting Standards (AS), not Ind AS. ₹ crore unless specified; group financials and fully owned group forecasts are separated from comparable parent growth. Dated secondary 19 October close ₹247.30 is not live or exchange-verified. Five annual steps, 15% nominal equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh analytical position. All four gates are Conditional with specific reasons, not automatic critical holds. History and conditional valuation are medium-confidence; executable market depth is not established.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 6, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 3, BAL 7, EXEC 5 and EARN 5 produce BQS 4.98. Raw GQS is 5.40, capped at 5 because weak cash conversion persists across years. R 7 follows 18.9066% base IRR minus 15%=3.9066 percentage points; D 5, P 5 and L 4 remain distinct judgments. IAS 5.60 uses Q 25%, R 35%, D 20%, P 10%, L 10% without reweighting. The narrow R band is sensitive to forecast error, not a precise expected payoff; all scores have stated counterevidence. No material input is silently filled as an observed fact.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Chemkart distributes and processes ingredients used in nutrition, health supplements and related applications. Commercial economics depend on supplier access, application knowledge, inventory availability and customers converting formulations into repeat orders. Existing blending and grinding activities differ from the still-developing manufacturing project. Easy Raw Materials and Vinstar are wholly owned subsidiaries at March 2026; parent growth is not inflated by adding their revenue twice. Vinstar FY26 turnover ₹2.2343 crore and loss ₹0.2472 crore explain the small revenue scope difference, while Easy Raw Materials reported no turnover and loss ₹0.5947 crore. Subscription cash moved into these entities is eliminated in the group model, not counted again as external project expenditure.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Technical distribution relationships and formulation support can differentiate service, but the prospectus does not establish durable exclusive suppliers or long-term customer purchase commitments. FY25 top-ten customers represented 45.91%; that dated measure is not presented as a FY26 concentration statistic. Ingredient substitution, international sourcing, customer bargaining and currency/customs changes can compress margins or tie up stock. Camlin Fine Sciences supplies a broad ingredient/chemical comparison, not a matched multiple: FY26 continuing revenue ₹1723.31 crore and core EBITDA ₹106.88 crore imply 6.20% margin, versus Chemkart 13.12%. Camlin owner continuing losses versus positive total profit from discontinued items demonstrate why headline P/E or gross margins cannot be transferred mechanically. Manufacturing scale and geographic scope differ materially.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Parent revenue FY23/24/25/26 was ₹131.3778/₹132.0269/₹203.2785/₹212.5948 crore. The comparable three-year CAGR is 17.40%; FY26 parent growth slowed to 4.58%, while group revenue ₹214.8291 crore rose 5.68%. FY22₹86.9805 crore offers an older diagnostic, but a verified five-year comparable series is not forced from an unverified FY21 base. Restated owner PAT FY23/24/25₹7.6602/₹14.5183/₹24.2709 differs from statutory owner ₹7.9721/₹13.9375/₹24.5325 because of disclosed adjustments. FY25 restated total group PAT is ₹24.2575 crore before its small negative minority result; owner PAT is ₹24.2709 crore. FY26 group owner PAT ₹19.6582 is compared with statutory prior owner ₹24.5325, not silently spliced into restated scope. July management reports Q1 FY27 sales ₹99.6022 crore,15 new customers and 20 R&D products; neither a quarterly margin/cash statement nor automatic four-times annualisation is assumed.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The manufacturing object is ₹34.6833 crore. March use ₹4.57 crore and June cumulative ₹7.09 crore leave ₹27.59 crore at June, not a second pool added to March cash. The newsletter reports completed plinth and power approval with machinery selection/order lead times; this is not proof of commissioning, utilization or return on capital. Historical prospectus ROCE 43%/51%/49% uses its disclosed closing-capital definition. FY26 core EBIT ₹27.6803 crore over closing equity plus debt gives 20.55%, not average-capital or incremental-project ROCE; IPO capital and unfinished assets change the denominator. Base sales reach ₹493.08 crore in FY31 through 35%/20%/15%/12%/10% annual growth, with 13% EBITDA margin. Lower growth, 10% margin and higher WC tests expose the risk that sales expansion consumes rather than releases owner cash.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The promoter-led operating structure and related-party dealings require specific economic review rather than generic reassurance. The annual remuneration disclosures total approximately ₹0.90 crore for the three executive family roles versus ₹0.855 crore previously; group intercompany funding is not automatically leakage. The secretarial report records a delayed half-year related-party disclosure and a paid exchange fine. The monitoring report separately describes ₹13.69 crore OFS transfers plus ₹2.20 crore related expenses, totaling ₹15.89 crore against ₹15.60 crore OFS, an additional ₹0.29 crore outflow. This is a bounded allocation issue requiring reconciliation, not proof of wider diversion. Its headline no-deviation wording must be read with the qualifications. The annual approximately ₹9.80 crore GCP line mathematically combines GCP and issue expenses; the final prospectus allocates only ₹0.2674 crore GCP. No unsupported ₹9.80 crore free-cash reserve is credited.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Restated FY23–25 CFO totals ₹4.0051 crore versus ₹46.4360 crore group profit, about8.63% conversion. FY26 actual CFO −₹2.7253 crore and cash capex ₹4.8683 crore give FCF−₹7.5936 crore. Adding back paid customs ₹14.7426 yields a diagnostic ₹12.0173 crore CFO before that payment, not cash recovered or free for distribution. The auditor emphasizes pending customs recovery and an omitted ₹1.10 crore sales transaction expected to be recognized in May, explicitly below overall materiality; the opinion is unmodified and subsequent recognition is unverified. Statutory/restated FY25 cash-flow differences retain the same net cash change and closing balance, so they are not described as missing cash. Opening tax payable ₹2.7278 crore is excluded from operating WC and paid once FY27; other current provisions ₹0.9157 crore remain in WC. Government asset ₹0.5972 crore is conservatively excluded pending composition/recovery, without a second refund credit. Restricted LC/FD balances and earmarked project funds are separated from free cash.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹247.30 and12,099,000 shares, market capitalization is ₹299.2083 crore, about15.22× FY26 owner PAT. No OFS cash belongs to the company and the fresh IPO is already in March assets. Group available bank/liquid funds ₹37.2782 crore are split into ₹30.1133 crore project reserve and ₹7.1649 crore free cash. Bear/base/bull cases use explicit annual sales paths,10%/13%/16% EBITDA margins,40%/33%/28% NWC, ₹25/₹30.1133/₹40 crore remaining project expenditure and7/10/13× exit EV/EBITDA. Conditional bear/base/bull terminal prices ₹192.38/₹587.77/₹1567.98 imply annual returns -4.90%/18.90%/44.68%. Annual rows fund opening tax, a ₹0.45 crore remaining issue-cost allowance, WC, maintenance and project capex, with half-year new-draw interest solved jointly with tax and year-end repayments. Customs recovery is zero in main cases; unused earmarked funds are not terminal surplus. Main peak debts ₹14.4989/₹5.5607/₹4.9528 crore are mathematical requirements, not verified October facilities. Multiples and asset lives are analyst estimates, not contemporaneous peer-derived fair values. The opening-claim bridge does not pay the ₹0.9157 crore non-tax current provisions twice because they are already in WC, and retains ₹0.080300 crore of net noncurrent employee/deposit claims as a terminal equity deduction. It does not force noncurrent claims into immediate repayment. Future operating compensation is cash funded with the opening net deficit held constant; existing taxes, capital creditors and normal WC liabilities are not charged twice.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The linked failure path is customer loss or repricing → slow inventory and receivables → funds tied in an unfinished factory → reserve depletion and refinancing → dilution or loss of equity value. The severe case combines 10% initial revenue decline, 6% margin,50% NWC, ₹40 crore completion cash,15% financing,₹10 crore reserve unavailability,₹6.9452 crore replacement/collection cash shock and a separately hypothetical ₹5 crore new customs demand. It requires peak debt ₹63.7660 crore. The disclosed ₹32 crore working-capital sanction and ₹4.8508 crore drawn balance are dated reference figures, not a promise of unused October drawing power. Non-recovery of already-paid customs is not paid again; only the explicitly hypothetical incremental demand adds cash. Separate recovery, dilution, margin, collection and capex sensitivities isolate drivers. BSE low × volume exit is 6.61 days at 5% observed participation, or 7.35 days under a conditional two-zero-gap case; circuits, depth and coarse lots can make actual exit much worse. With all identified opening claims included, severe peak required debt is ₹63.7660 crore and terminal price is ₹0.0000; these are conditional requirements, not committed facilities.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold/tenfold equity values from the dated quote require approximately ₹1496 crore/₹2992 crore. At an illustrative 20× P/E and 10% net margin, required profit is ₹74.8 crore/₹149.6 crore and revenue ₹748 crore/₹1496 crore before debt, dilution and cash adjustments. From current group revenue ₹214.83 crore, that implies roughly 28%/47% annual growth for five years. The bull model reaches a high multiple of the current share price only through sustained strong growth, 16% margins, lower WC intensity and successful completion; it is not independent evidence that a multibagger is likely. Tenfold requires substantially more scale or valuation than the base model establishes. Manufacturing execution, supplier access, customers and cash conversion must improve together.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Next reporting cycle: reconcile auditor-highlighted sales recognition and customs status to ledgers and cash, without assuming a favorable outcome. Quarterly proceeds reports: reconcile GCP/investment income, OFS-related allocation, project invoices, remaining expenses and liquid-fund availability. Plant milestones: actual orders, delivery, commissioning, customer qualification and utilization rather than civil-construction progress alone. Operating triggers: parent revenue growth, EBITDA margin near the 13% base, receivable aging, inventory turnover and cumulative CFO/PAT; persistent WC above 40% or margin near 10% weakens the base return. Funding triggers: net tax settlement, actual drawing power and accessible sanctioned limits. Market checks before any order: BSE board/lot/surveillance, live bid depth, spread and circuit queues, with lot-aware position sizing.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed applicable review: conditional growth-and-execution watchlist, not an established high-quality cash compounder. BQS 4.98 and capped GQS 5.00 separate business quality from forecast upside. Conditional IAS 5.60 is rankable only within this framework and its disclosed dated-price/assumption limits; it is not a buy instruction or assurance of liquidity. The base has a sufficient explicit budget and funded bridge for a medium-confidence R 7 estimate rather than blanket NS, but a small change in assumptions can move the return band. No allocation is recommended before checking actual cash deployment, project progress and executable trading conditions. Missing evidence is retained in the relevant gates and sensitivities, not hidden behind precision.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The revised issuer annual report and final prospectus control financial scope; original provision/PPE and monitoring allocation/progress layouts were inspected. Older issuer reports and prospectus restatements were reviewed where available; one purported FY24 download duplicated FY23 and is not counted as independent financial coverage. September subsidiary subscription was read from an issuer-letter transcription after the exchange attachment failed, so it supports a bounded ownership/event update, not full-event clearance. Camlin’s original annual financials were read for a narrow economic comparison. Secondary OHLCV is explicitly not actual turnover or live depth. Open gaps are current customs outcome, completed sales-cutoff correction, actual October cash/WC and drawing power, final project invoices/useful lives, FY26 customer/supplier concentration and executable BSE liquidity. These do not prevent the supportable annual funded analysis, but remain material decision conditions. Opening claims are reconciled separately: current exclusions settle once, normal operating balances remain in WC, and net noncurrent employee/deposit claims reduce terminal equity without an unsupported immediate-payout assumption.

GOV.reason: Audited disclosures and monitored proceeds provide a usable control trail. Contrary: the specific OFS allocation qualification, paid filing fine, cutoff and customs uncertainty require follow-through; neither allegations nor minor issues are treated as proven diversion.

MOAT.reason: Product/application knowledge and blending support distribution relationships. Contrary: no established exclusive supply or durable contracted demand; international ingredient competition and customer bargaining constrain durable pricing power.

REV.reason: Comparable parent three-year CAGR 17.4024% starts at band 7, reduced one point for FY26 parent growth 4.58% and uncertain recurrence of the management Q1 surge. Five-year comparable revenue unavailable; parent and acquired group scopes separated.

DUR.reason: Nutrition ingredient demand, product pipeline and new manufacturing offer a medium-duration runway. Contrary: pipeline is not contracted sales, top-ten concentration 45.91% is dated FY25, and new factory economics remain unproved.

CAP.reason: Historical reported ROCE 43–51% supports trading economics, but uses closing defined capital rather than incremental returns. IPO-funded capital and unfinished factory reduce comparability; new-project returns and working-capital efficiency are unproved.

CASH.reason: Restated FY23–25 CFO totals 4.0051 crore against 46.4360 crore group PAT, a persistent weak-conversion pattern; FY26 actual CFO is negative. Customs payment explains much of latest cash pressure but is paid cash, not an automatic recovery. Persistent CASH 3 caps GQS at 5.

BAL.reason: Gross debt 4.9528 is modest against equity 129.7298, with 7.1649 free-cash proxy after project earmarking. Contrary: customs asset 14.7426, restricted balances, WC and project funding prevent treating headline 38.6454 cash as surplus. Severe refinancing requirement is explicit.

EXEC.reason: IPO debt repayment and project spending are evidenced; management Q1 sales and construction milestones are encouraging. Contrary: commissioning, customer recurrence and completed project returns are not established; slower spending is not itself successful execution.

EARN.reason: Operating earnings remain substantive and other income is small. Contrary: statutory owner PAT declined, core margins compressed, and cutoff/customs assets qualify quality; statutory and restated prior profits are not silently spliced.

R.reason: Conditional base IRR 18.9040% minus 15% hurdle=+3.9040 percentage points, the 2–4 point band 7. Medium-confidence assumption estimate: explicit monitored project budget, opening-tax settlement, no customs recovery and bounded financing paths support a score, not an actionable forecast. Q1 management revenue is not annualized fourfold; lower-margin/collection/overrun cases are material counterevidence.

D.reason: Low opening leverage and conservative exclusion of customs recovery provide resilience. Contrary: base/bear funding must be supported, while severe joint demand/WC/reserve/customs stress needs 63.7660 crore debt against only a dated32 crore sanction reference. Survivability cannot be inferred from a mathematical draw.

P.reason: Static owner earnings multiple 15.22× is not extreme, and a funded base exceeds15% hurdle; however the result needs sustained cash conversion, roughly13% margin and project execution. Margins, multiples and collection assumptions can remove the apparent upside; no automatic cheapness from liquid funds.

L.reason: Low×volume observed exit 6.61 days at 5%, or 7.35 days under a conditional two-zero-gap case, both start at band 5. One-point downgrade for coarse600-share lots, secondary proxy/provider gaps and absent live depth. Medium-confidence conditional capacity estimate, not BSE surveillance clearance or an execution guarantee.

valuation.interest_timing_convention: New borrowing incurs half-year interest in the year drawn. Ordinary excess-cash repayments occur at year-end and receive no same-year interest saving. Curis collateral-funded FD overdraft repayment retains its explicit half-year timing. Interest, positive-profit cash tax and funding draw are solved jointly to a 1e-12 crore tolerance; new borrowing is a funding requirement, not a committed facility.
valuation.formulas: Group revenue follows five explicit annual growth assumptions, not mechanical four-times extrapolation of the management Q1 update. EBITDA is scenario margin times sales. Depreciation starts from 0.4965 and adds 8% of cumulative prior model capex plus half-year 8% on current project capex, limited to available assets; this is a commissioning proxy, not an audited useful-life schedule. Tax is 26% of positive EBITDA less depreciation and solved financing cost. CFO deducts interest, tax on forecast profit, the opening net tax settlement and full operating NWC change. Annual cash separately pays remaining project capex (70% FY27, 30% FY28), maintenance 1.5% of revenue, the opening net tax liability and a 0.45 remaining issue-cost allowance. Project reserve is part of March cash, not extra proceeds; it releases only against project payments. June project expenditure is part of full FY27 spending and not added a second time. Parent subscriptions into wholly owned subsidiaries are eliminated from group funding and not paid again alongside project capex. Existing CWIP and capital advances are not separately repaid. Current principal 0.102 is included in opening debt and modelled as annual year-end runoff, with refinancing explicitly drawn if needed. New draws bear half-year interest and are solved jointly with tax. Other repayments are year-end, with a free cash floor of 2. No new shares or equity proceeds in main cases. Terminal equity=group EBITDA×multiple−debt+free cash; remaining earmarked reserve, restricted deposits and unrecovered customs asset are excluded. Customs recovery sensitivities credit cash once in FY28; non-recovery/impairment alone is noncash because duty was already paid. Additional-demand stresses are hypothetical incremental cash calls, not disclosed new liabilities. Opening-claim extension: first-year CFO includes the separately settled opening tax and excluded current employee/interest claims. Previously accrued taxes and capital creditors are not paid twice. Old unpaid dividends are financing cash outflows without new buyer entitlement. Net noncurrent employee/deposit claims reduce terminal equity once, while normal WC liabilities remain within the operating cash bridge.
limitations: March balances plus a specified annual path are not verified October net debt. Actual interim working capital and proceeds deployment remain uncertain.

Remaining project spending of 25/30.1133/40 brackets the monitored object budget and possible completion/overlap uncertainty. The 0.6945 paid capital advance is not paid again separately, but its precise reconciliation to object utilisation needs invoice-level evidence.

The June monitor reports 7.09 cumulative project use and 27.59 remaining, versus March 4.57 and 30.1133. Neither June cash balances nor post-March intercompany subscriptions are added to March group cash.

The annual report groups roughly 9.80 of GCP and issue expenses; the final prospectus separates 0.2674 and 9.5293. The model does not invent a 9.80 discretionary cash reserve. The 0.45 issue-cost allowance is conservatively paid, not represented as a verified payable.

A disclosed 32.00 working-capital sanction and 4.8508 drawn balance provide a dated reference, not proof of October drawing-power availability or undrawn committed headroom. Model draws above accessible facilities require refinancing.

Customs recoverability remains disputed and no recovery is included in main cases. Full impairment changes book equity, not a second cash payment; only separately labelled incremental-demand scenarios add new cash outflow.

Quarterly revenue and improved-margin statements in the July newsletter are management reports without a reviewed quarterly cash or detailed margin statement. Manufacturing commissioning and asset lives remain estimates.
Terminal multiples are analyst assumptions. Secondary price-volume history is not actual traded value or live depth, and BSE surveillance clearance is not established.
